messages.subject: repoducing plot on page 30 of book
parts:
On the bottom of page 30 of the ggplot2 book, there are two plots. I find it easy to reproduce the first, but get an error when I try to reproduce the second.

> data(mpg)
> qplot(displ, hwy, data = mpg, geom = "line", colour = factor(cyl)) ## Works fine
> qplot(displ, hwy, data = mpg, geom = "bar", colour = factor(cyl))
stat_bin: binwidth defaulted to range/30. Use 'binwidth = x' to adjust this.
Error in Ops.data.frame(mmm, each) : list of length 14462 not meaningful
In addition: Warning message:
In cbind(is.na(mmm), is.na(each)) :
number of rows of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 2)
>

Am I doing something wrong?

Thanks,

Dave

> In addition: Warning message:

> number of rows of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 2)

I get a different error than you; I get

> qplot(displ, hwy, data=mpg, colour=factor(cyl), geom="bar")
stat_bin: binwidth defaulted to range/30. Use 'binwidth = x' to adjust this.

I can reproduce the graph with

qplot(displ, hwy, data=mpg, colour=factor(cyl), geom="bar",
stat="identity", position="identity")

I can't really say you were doing something wrong, because the graph is
an example of how you can create syntactically valid nonsense; you just
created different syntactically valid nonsense.

> Thanks,
>

messages.author: 68b661fcb57b94a9
messages.subject: Re: repoducing plot on page 30 of book
parts:
Wasn't sure if anyone responded already to your question, but here's a solution. The key is to change the stat from the default, which counts in one dimension to "identity", so that it can use hwy on the y-axis. Also, to reproduce the plot on page 30, you need to change the position from the default, which is "stacked", to be, "dodge," so the cases lay side by side. Hope this helps.  It's probably a good sign it wasn't obvious how to reproduce this plot since it doesn't make any sense really.

ggplot(mpg,aes(displ,hwy,colour=factor(cyl)))+geom_bar(aes(fill=factor(cyl)),stat="identity", position="dodge")





Adam Loveland
